$comment: Curated game events the extractor cannot see.
Every entry here fires in real GOTV demos and appears in the
CMsgSource1LegacyGameEventList descriptor, but is declared nowhere in
gameevents_schema.json or the SchemaTracker artifact it derives from. See
This file is ADDITIVE ONLY. If the extracted schema gains one of these
names, generation fails with CS2_GEN_008 and the entry must be DELETED —
the real declaration wins, and a curated guess must never shadow it.
The field lists are OBSERVED, not declared. Type tags are copied from the
nearest extracted neighbour (item_pickup / item_equip / item_remove) so the
generated factory emits the same reader call the sibling events use.
'source' is not settable: the generator stamps sdk.supplement.

fields.name: userid
fields.comment: the player who dropped the item

fields.name: item
fields.comment: either a weapon such as 'tmp' or 'hegrenade', or an item such as 'nvgs'

annotations.description: Fired when a player drops a weapon or item.
annotations.notes: Field shapes mirror `item_pickup`, `item_equip` and `item_remove`, which the schema does declare: `userid` is a controller slot and `item` is the classname / definition string. The descriptor may carry keys beyond these two; only the observed pair is modelled.

annotations.description: Fired at the half-time side switch.
annotations.notes: A separate native name from `start_halftime`, which the schema does declare. No keys were observed on it, so the record is empty — an empty record is still worth having, because it is what lets a dispatcher see the fire at all.
No keys were observed on it, so the record is empty. Distinct from `round_start`, which marks a new round within an ongoing game.
